identificationModule.briefTitle: Chimeric Antigen-Receptor-Modified T Cells Targeting B7-H3
identificationModule.officialTitle: Chimeric Antigen-Receptor-Modified T Cells Targeting B7-H3 for the Treatment of High-Grade Gliomas (Sonia's Trial)

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
LCCC 2534-ATL is an early-stage (Phase 1), single-center clinical study evaluating the safety of CAR T-cell therapy in children and adults with high-grade gliomas (HGGs), which are aggressive brain cancers.

The treatment, called iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells, uses modified immune cells designed to recognize and attack cancer cells with a protein called B7-H3. The treatment also includes a safety switch (iC9) designed to help stop the modified cells if serious side effects occur.

Earlier studies of B7-H3-targeted CAR T-cell therapy have shown encouraging safety results, with some patients experiencing tumor shrinkage. This study will further evaluate the safety and tolerability of the treatment in children and adults with high-grade gliomas type brain tumors.

The study will use a 3+3 dose-escalation design to evaluate increasing doses and identify the safest appropriate dose. The results will help determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D), which is the dose selected for further study.

Participants who qualify will have blood collected to produce the modified T cells. Three treatment doses will be administered two weeks apart. Additional doses may be given.

Participants will be monitored for 15 years after treatment ends or is discontinued to assess potential long-term side effects related to genetic modification of the cells.

interventions.name: iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells therapy
interventions.description: Participants receive increasing doses of genetically modified immune cells (iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells) to evaluate safety and determine the recommended dose for future studies.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants Experiencing Treatment-Related Adverse Events (AEs) in adults (Cohort A).
primaryOutcomes.description: Number of Participants Experiencing Treatment-Related Grade ≥3 Adverse Events (AEs) in adults will be classified and graded according to the National Cancer Institute's Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE), Version 6.0.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Cytokine Release Syndrome in adults (Cohort A)
primaryOutcomes.description:
Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS) will be graded according to American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT) CRS Consensus Grading. Grade ≥ 3 Adverse Events (AEs) will be reported.

Grade 1 - Mild (Symptomatic Management): Fever ≥38\^ o C, No hypotension, No hypoxia, Grade 2 - Moderate (Moderate Intervention): Fever ≥38\^ o C, Hypotension not requiring vasopressors, Hypoxia requiring low-flow nasal cannula (≤6 L/minute) or blow-by, Grade 3 - Severe (Aggressive Intervention): Fever ≥ 38\^ o C , Hypotension requiring a vasopressor with or without vasopressin, Hypoxia requiring high-flow nasal cannula (\>6 L/minute), facemask, nonrebreather mask, or Venturi mask, Grade 4 - Life-threatening (Life-sustaining intervention): Fever ≥38\^oC, Hypotension requiring multiple vasopressors (excluding vasopressin),Hypoxia requiring positive pressure (e.g. Continuous positive airway pressure, BiPAP, intubation, mechanical ventilation), Grade 5 - Death: Death.

Neurotoxicity will be graded according to the Central Nervous System (CNS) Toxicity criteria. Grade ≥ 3 Adverse Events (AEs) will be reported.

Grade 0: Normal or no change from baseline exam at start of therapy, Grade 1: Mild lethargy and/or irritability or visual, motor, or sensory symptoms without change in neurological exam, Grade 2: Moderate lethargy, disorientation, or psychosis lasting \< 48 hours or mild increase in pre-existing neurological deficit, Grade 3: \>48hours of severe lethargy, but responsive to verbal stimuli or disorientation or psychosis lasting \>48 hours, Grade 4: Coma, unresponsive to verbal stimuli, increasing neurological deficit above grade 3, evidence of herniation, development of uncontrolled seizures, intracerebral hemorrhage.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Treatment-Induced Adverse Neurological Events (TIAN) in adults (Cohort A)
primaryOutcomes.description: Treatment-Induced Adverse Neurological Events (TIAN) will be classified and graded according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI CTCAE) Version 6.0. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) will be reported. TIAN severity will be assessed using the applicable CTCAE v6.0 criteria.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Treatment-Induced Adverse Neurological Events (TIAN) in Pediatrics (Cohort B)
primaryOutcomes.description: Treatment-Induced Adverse Neurological Events (TIAN) will be classified and graded per protocol-specific criteria; Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) will be reported. Grade 1 (mild): Headache with fever \>38°C or mild worsening of pre-existing neurological signs/symptoms causing minor functional deficits, requiring observation or symptomatic management only. Grade 2 (moderate): Moderate neurological examination changes from baseline substantially affecting function (e.g., new/worsening hemiparesis, ataxia limiting walking, or cranial neuropathies limiting eating). Grade 3 (severe): Severe neurological signs/symptoms potentially affecting critical cardiorespiratory functions, or increased intracranial pressure (ICP) \>20 mmHg responsive to intervention. Grade 4 (life-threatening).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) in adults (Cohort A)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells will be determined using modified 3+3 dose-escalation rules. Tolerability will be assessed using the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE), version 6.0, and the American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT) criteria for cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Neurotoxicity will be assessed using the Treatment-Induced Adverse Neurological Events (TIAN) criteria.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: The disease control rate (DCR) in adults (Cohort A)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The disease control rate (DCR) is the proportion of subjects who achieve a complete response (CR), partial response (PR), or stable disease (SD), as defined in the protocol. Complete response (CR) is defined as the disappearance of all target lesions. Partial response (PR) is defined as at least a 50% decrease in the sum of the products of the two perpendicular diameters of all target lesions compared with baseline measurements. Stable disease (SD) is defined as neither a sufficient decrease in tumor size to qualify as a partial response nor a sufficient increase to qualify as progressive disease (PD).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Feasibility of procuring and manufacturing iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells in adults (Cohort A)
secondaryOutcomes.description: To evaluate the feasibility of procuring and manufacturing iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells. Procurement feasibility will be measured as the proportion of individuals who successfully undergo procurement among those who attempt it. Manufacturing feasibility will be measured as the proportion of successfully procured individuals for whom the cells are successfully manufactured to provide three doses.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria

* Provide written informed consent/assent and HIPAA authorization, signed by the subject, parent/guardian, or legally authorized representative, after the study information has been explained and understood.
* Meet the age requirements at consent/assent:

  * Adult cohort: ≥18 years.
  * Pediatric cohort: ≥2 and \<18 years, with a minimum body weight of 10 kg at enrollment.
* Karnofsky performance status ≥50 (\>16 years) or Lansky performance status ≥50 (≤16 years). Participants unable to walk because of paralysis but able to sit upright in a wheelchair will be considered ambulatory for performance assessment.
* Subjects with newly diagnosed non-pontine DMG may enroll following completion of standard radiotherapy and prior to documented disease progression.
* Unless otherwise specified, subjects must meet all the following criteria to participate in any phase of the study:
* Histologically or radiographically diagnosed high-grade glioma, including:

  * Recurrent or progressive pediatric-type diffuse high-grade glioma.
  * Recurrent or progressive adult-type diffuse grade 4 glioma.
  * Diffuse midline glioma (DMG), H3 K27-altered, after completion of standard radiotherapy.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Subjects have presence of clinical and/or radiographic evidence of impending herniation and/or impending spinal cord compression.
* Pontine diffuse midline glioma (including diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma \[DIPG\]).
* Clinical or radiographic evidence of impending herniation and/or impending spinal cord compression.
